bookTitle: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets

facts.statement: Dow published the first stock average in 1884 with 11 stocks, subsequently splitting it into a 12-stock Industrial index and a 20-stock Rail index in 1897 to better gauge economic health.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Dow Theory: The 6 Basic Tenets & 3 Trend Classifications
sourceCitation.excerpt: Dow divided the market into two distinct indices: a 12-stock Industrial index and a 20-stock Rail index to better reflect economic health [3].

facts.statement: An uptrend is strictly defined as a sequence of successively higher peaks and higher troughs, whereas a downtrend requires systematically lower peaks and lower troughs based on action and reaction.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Dow Theory: The 6 Basic Tenets & 3 Trend Classifications
sourceCitation.excerpt: An uptrend is defined as a series of successively higher peaks and higher troughs... downtrend is defined as a series of lower peaks and lower troughs [8].

facts.statement: Market index averages instantaneously assimilate and reflect all fundamental knowledge, market sentiment, and unforeseen natural acts of God through the pure forces of supply and demand acting on asset prices.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Dow Theory: The 6 Basic Tenets & 3 Trend Classifications
sourceCitation.excerpt: Supply and demand forces automatically assimilate all fundamental factors, market sentiment, and even unforeseen 'acts of God'... into the price action almost instantaneously [6].

facts.statement: The primary trend, metaphorically analogous to an ocean tide, represents the major directional movement lasting over one year in equity markets and longer than six months in futures markets.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Dow Theory: The 6 Basic Tenets & 3 Trend Classifications
sourceCitation.excerpt: Lasts more than one year (often several years) in stock markets [13]. In futures markets, major trends are shortened to anything over six months [14].

facts.statement: Secondary trends act as counter-trend corrections within a primary move, lasting between three weeks to three months and typically retracing one-third to two-thirds of the preceding primary wave's advance.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Dow Theory: The 6 Basic Tenets & 3 Trend Classifications
sourceCitation.excerpt: Lasts three weeks to three months... Typically retraces between 33.3% and 66.6% (1/3 to 2/3) of the preceding primary advance or decline [13].

facts.statement: Minor trends, acting as near-term ripples within an intermediate secondary wave, last less than three weeks and are primarily utilized by market participants for tactical trade execution and precision timing.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Dow Theory: The 6 Basic Tenets & 3 Trend Classifications
sourceCitation.excerpt: Short-term fluctuations within the intermediate wave... Lasts less than three weeks... Used primarily for trade execution and timing [15, 16].

facts.statement: The initial accumulation phase occurs at the nadir of a bear market when informed smart money absorbs shares, as negative economic news is fully discounted by severely depressed market sentiment.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Dow Theory: The 6 Basic Tenets & 3 Trend Classifications
sourceCitation.excerpt: Occurs at the tail end of a bear market when market sentiment is exceedingly depressed and bad economic news has been fully discounted [9].

facts.statement: The public participation phase experiences rapidly advancing asset prices fueled by trend-following technical traders and institutions entering the market as underlying business indicators and corporate fundamentals definitively improve.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Dow Theory: The 6 Basic Tenets & 3 Trend Classifications
sourceCitation.excerpt: Characterized by rapidly advancing prices, improving business indicators, and widespread public interest... trend-following technical traders and institutional participants [9].

facts.statement: During the final distribution phase, original early accumulators systematically sell their holdings to an overly optimistic general public amid glowing media reports, peak economic data, and extremely heavy speculative volume.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Dow Theory: The 6 Basic Tenets & 3 Trend Classifications
sourceCitation.excerpt: Accompanied by glowing media reports, peak economic indicators, heavy speculative volume... Astute early accumulators who distribute (sell) their holdings to the general public [9].

facts.statement: A major trend reversal signal remains completely invalid unless the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the Transportation Average successfully penetrate prior secondary peaks or troughs, generating matching structural signals together.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Dow Theory: The 6 Basic Tenets & 3 Trend Classifications
sourceCitation.excerpt: No major bull or bear market signal is valid unless both the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the Dow Jones Transportation Average generate matching signals [10].

facts.statement: Trading volume must definitively expand in the direction of the primary trend, meaning activity increases during rallies and actively contracts during dips in a bull market, serving as a critical secondary indicator.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Dow Theory: The 6 Basic Tenets & 3 Trend Classifications
sourceCitation.excerpt: Trading activity should expand in the direction of the primary trend: in an uptrend, volume increases as prices rise and contracts on dips [11].

facts.statement: Rooted inherently in physical laws of momentum, Dow Theory assumes an existing market trend remains dynamically in force and will continue advancing until an external fundamental force generates a definitive reversal signal.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Dow Theory: The 6 Basic Tenets & 3 Trend Classifications
sourceCitation.excerpt: Based on physical laws of momentum, an existing market trend tends to remain in motion until an external force generates a clear reversal signal [12].

facts.statement: Secondary corrections predictably retrace calculable geometric portions of the prior primary wave's advance, determined mathematically using specific fraction multipliers applied tightly against the peak-to-trough range of the previous impulse move.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Dow Theory: The 6 Basic Tenets & 3 Trend Classifications
sourceCitation.excerpt: Dow Theory uses specific percentage boundaries to measure secondary corrections [13].

variables.definition: Highest closing price of the prior primary wave
Lowest closing price of the prior primary wave

facts.statement: If a primary index wave advances aggressively from a 10,000 trough to a 12,000 peak, the subsequent secondary counter-trend correction typically retraces 50% (a 1,000 point drop) before forcefully resuming the trend.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Dow Theory: The 6 Basic Tenets & 3 Trend Classifications
sourceCitation.excerpt: A 50% retracement of the prior move represents the single most common correction distance [13].

generalAssumptions: Market action discounts all known and unknown fundamentals.
Prices move in trends, and a trend in motion is more likely to continue than to reverse.
